note: Permanent regression corpus for zig-audio. Every sample is built by src/fuzz_corpus_gen.zig, embedded into the test binary with @embedFile, and replayed by src/fuzz_corpus_test.zig. `stage` says where the expected error must appear: open = root.open must return it; read = root.open must succeed and the first failing read must return it.

samples.name: ogg_bos_continued
samples.construction: A structurally valid BOS page (correct CRC, one 19-byte OpusHead lace) with the continued flag set. A BOS page may not continue a previous page.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks the BOS/continued contradiction at the first page

samples.name: ogg_page_body_short
samples.construction: Page header with segment_count=2 and laces {10,20}, but only ten body bytes follow. The body read must stop at EOF, not loop.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks the lace-sum versus body-length boundary

samples.name: ogg_page_crc
samples.construction: A valid single-lace OpusHead BOS page whose stored CRC is 0xDEADBEEF instead of the Ogg CRC-32 of the page.
samples.symptom: none observed; the CRC check stays mandatory on every page

samples.name: ogg_eof_mid_packet
samples.construction: A complete Opus head page and tags page, then a final EOS page containing one 255-byte lace and no terminating lace below 255. The packet is still open when the physical stream ends.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks packet continuation across page and EOF

samples.name: ogg_sequence_gap
samples.construction: Head page sequence 0, tags page sequence 1, audio page sequence 3. The packet is valid but one page is missing.
samples.symptom: none observed; a skipped page is not silently accepted

samples.name: opus_toc_one_byte
samples.construction: A valid Ogg Opus file whose only audio packet is the single byte 0x03: frame count code 3 requires at least two bytes.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks RFC 6716 [R6,R7] on the shortest possible packet

samples.name: opus_toc_code1_odd
samples.construction: TOC 0x01 (code 1, two CBR frames) plus one payload byte. N-1 must be even.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks [R3] parity

samples.name: opus_toc_count_zero
samples.construction: TOC 0x03 plus a frame-count byte of 0. At least one frame is required.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks the zero-frame count

samples.name: opus_toc_too_long
samples.construction: TOC 0x03, config 0 (SILK NB 10 ms = 480 samples), frame count 13. 13 * 480 = 6240 > the 5760-sample / 120 ms cap.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks [R5] at the exact first count above the boundary

samples.name: flac_frame_truncated
samples.construction: A valid 44.1 kHz mono 16-bit FLAC with one 32-sample CONSTANT frame, truncated by four bytes: the frame header is intact and the bit reader hits EOF before the footer.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks the valid-prefix-then-Truncated rule

samples.name: flac_header_truncated
samples.construction: The same FLAC truncated three bytes into the frame header, after the sync code but before the coded number and header CRC.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks byte-at-a-time header reads at EOF

samples.name: flac_wasted_overrun
samples.construction: A valid frame header followed by a subframe byte 0x01 (pad 0, CONSTANT, wasted-bits flag 1) and four zero bytes. readUnary(31) reaches 32 zero bits and must return Corrupt instead of scanning to the 24-bit protection limit.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks the wasted-bits unary cap and proves the cap is below any unbounded scan

samples.name: aiff_comm_short
samples.source: constructed by src/fuzz_corpus_gen.zig (AIFF big-endian length class)
samples.construction: FORM/AIFF with a COMM chunk whose big-endian size field is 12, below the 18-byte minimum.
samples.symptom: none observed; a short COMM is not read past its declared size

samples.name: aiff_negative_rate
samples.source: constructed by src/fuzz_corpus_gen.zig (AIFF big-endian length class)
samples.construction: A valid COMM with the sign bit of the 80-bit extended sample rate set, plus a 4-byte SSND payload.
samples.symptom: none observed; a negative rate is named, not clamped to zero

samples.name: aiff_frames_exceed_ssnd
samples.source: constructed by src/fuzz_corpus_gen.zig (AIFF big-endian length class)
samples.construction: COMM declares 100 frames of mono 16-bit, but SSND carries only four payload bytes (two frames) after its 8-byte offset/block header. The first read returns two frames, the next names Truncated.
samples.symptom: none observed; locks COMM frame count versus SSND byte length

samples.name: aiff_ssnd_before_comm
samples.source: constructed by src/fuzz_corpus_gen.zig (AIFF big-endian length class)
samples.construction: SSND before COMM. A streaming decoder cannot rewind to the samples after learning the channel count and frame size.
samples.symptom: none observed; the refusal stays named instead of guessing

samples.name: adpcm_ima_step89
samples.construction: A two-block IMA ADPCM WAV (block_align 32). The first block header stores step_index 89; the table has 89 entries, indices 0..88.
samples.symptom: none observed; the one-past-the-end step index is rejected before the table read

samples.name: adpcm_ima_short_tail
samples.construction: block_align 32 with a data payload of 35 bytes: one full block plus a three-byte tail shorter than the four-byte IMA header.
samples.symptom: none observed; a short final block is Corrupt when the data size is declared, not silent EOF

samples.name: adpcm_ms_bad_predictor
samples.construction: Microsoft ADPCM with the standard seven coefficient pairs; the first block header's predictor index is 7, one past the last valid index 6.
samples.symptom: none observed; the coefficient table is indexed only after the range check

samples.name: adpcm_ms_block_align_short
samples.construction: A mono Microsoft ADPCM WAV with block_align 6, below the seven-byte per-channel block header.
samples.symptom: none observed; block_align is checked against the header size before any allocation
